citations.A1: `_cache` is filled on first call and never checked against the file again, so any on-disk edit is invisible for the process lifetime — record the file's `stat()` (`st_mtime_ns`, `st_size`) with the data and reload when it differs
citations.A2: NOT a fix — a TTL/time-based expiry: it only shrinks the stale window and still re-reads when nothing changed; staleness remains by design
citations.A3: NOT a fix — adding a `reload_config()` for callers to call: depends on every writer remembering, and does nothing when an editor or another process edits the file
citations.A4: The cache ignores `path`, so a second call with a different file returns the first file's contents — key the cache dict by the resolved absolute path
citations.A5: Two threads can enter the load (and, once reloading is added, swap `_cache` mid-read) — guard the stat-check-and-load with a `threading.Lock`
citations.A6: Callers get the shared mutable dict, so one caller's mutation silently becomes everyone's config and survives until reload — return a deep copy or a read-only mapping
